subdomain: 3.4 Analyze observability challenges and select monitoring strategies at scale

en.question: A contract-analysis service uses the Claude OpenTelemetry export beta documented on 2026-10-26. Central telemetry must not contain confidential customer text. Some dynamically generated agent and tool descriptions include customer names; approved redacted diagnostic examples may be stored separately with restricted access. Which monitoring decisions satisfy these constraints? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Review and sanitize names and descriptions before metadata-only export, not just prompt and response attributes.
options.note: Metadata-only mode still includes chosen descriptive text. Sensitive values in those fields can violate the policy even when complete prompts and responses are excluded.

options.text: Treat metadata-only mode as a guarantee that no customer text can reach the telemetry destination.
options.note: The documented metadata mode can include agent and tool names and descriptions. Its mode name is not a substitute for reviewing the actual exported attributes.

options.text: Collect only policy-approved, redacted diagnostic samples in the separate store with explicit access and retention controls.
options.note: Selective diagnostics can support investigation without enabling unrestricted transcript capture centrally. Redaction, destination access, and retention must satisfy the stated data-handling policy.

options.text: Export unredacted full content for a small random sample because low sampling rates satisfy the confidentiality rule.
options.note: Sampling reduces volume but still exports confidential text for sampled requests. A prohibition on such content is not converted into permission by lowering the sample rate.

references.title: Anthropic: OpenTelemetry tracing for the Claude API
